entities.summary: Admiral Sir John Borlase Warren, 1st Baronet was a Royal Navy officer, diplomat and politician who sat in the British House of Commons between 1774 and 1807. Born in 1748 in London, England, Warren rose through the ranks of the Royal Navy, becoming the Admiral of the Blue Squadron. He played a key role in the American Revolutionary War, serving as a naval aide to General Charles Cornwallis. Warren's diplomatic efforts helped to secure the Treaty of Paris, which ended the war. After the war, Warren served as the British Ambassador to the Netherlands and the United States. He was a strong advocate for the abolition of the slave trade and was a member of the Committee of the Privy Council for Trade and Plantations. Warren's contributions to the British Navy and his diplomatic efforts had a lasting impact on the development of the Royal Navy and the British Empire. He was a key figure in the development of the 'blue water' naval strategy and was instrumental in the establishment of the Royal Navy's supremacy at sea. Warren's legacy continues to be felt in the modern Royal Navy, and he remains one of the most important figures in the history of the British Navy.
